findings.claim: `build-manifest --check` does not run or enforce `agent-team-creator validate`, so an invalid `.agent-team/team.json` can pass the required check.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion: "`.agent-team/team.json` SHALL pass `agent-team-creator validate` ...; `build-manifest --check` fails otherwise." In `main()`, `problems` is built only from `rosterDocProblems`, `ownershipProblems`, `skillProblems`, `cardProblems`, `ownsStatementProblems`, and drift; no `cli.mjs validate` invocation or validation-result check is present.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `--check` invoke the recorded agent-team-creator CLI validate command against the generated manifest/team request, or embed the same validation as a required check and fail with its errors.

findings.claim: `fhir-test-engineer` grants itself write ownership outside its manifest `owns`, undermining the required disjoint ownership map.
findings.evidence: Header `owns` is only `[internal/testutil/**, internal/conformance/**, internal/store/testdata/**]`, but the prompt says it owns "`*_test.go` across the repo" and may edit production code for test seams; those paths overlap other roles' owns such as `fhir-go-developer` owning `internal/handler/**` and `fhir-storage-search-engineer` owning `internal/store/*.go`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add explicit, disjoint test-file ownership globs to the manifest and adjust other roles accordingly, or remove the broad `*_test.go`/test-seam permission and route package-local tests through the package-owning roles.
